Limitations: Prometheus local TSDB is not replicated; bound series churn, retention and query use. VictoriaMetrics has separate Enterprise features; MetricsQL compatibility and resource savings need workload tests.
MVP: Existing Prometheus; otherwise local Prometheus with bounded retention and local rules.
Enterprise: Benchmark VictoriaMetrics single-node locally and its cluster edition for approved central aggregates; retain local evaluation. No automatic migration solely because fleet reaches 10k.

Limitations: Filesystem queues consume disk and can overflow. OTel component stability varies; Vector has buffer minimums and experimental configurations. Host logs require sensitive mounts.
MVP: Fluent Bit for node logs; OTel only when OTLP/tracing or existing deployment justifies it.
Enterprise: Standardize one primary agent per signal; use minimal OTel distributions or Vector when transformations warrant it. Avoid duplicate collection.

Limitations: Loki needs explicit auth and label discipline; filesystem examples are not a production storage plan. OpenSearch adds JVM/index/replication operations. Both can store sensitive evidence.
MVP: Reuse local backend; otherwise evaluate Loki for stream/time queries with supported local-boundary storage. A VM prototype can query bounded local files.
Enterprise: OpenSearch only if indexed full-text needs justify cost; Loki with appropriate object storage/HA for larger customer clusters. No central raw-log lake under current privacy rule.

Limitations: Complementary host metrics, object state and node conditions; not interchangeable RCA engines. NPD writes conditions/events; exporter host access is privileged visibility.
MVP: Reuse existing exporters; add missing signals and vetted NPD checks.
Enterprise: Scope API watches/labels, test version support and reduce duplication with cloud-native node detection.

Limitations: Device/RAID passthrough differs; SMART does not predict every failure. Scrutiny describes itself as work in progress and adds a database/UI. Both require device access.
MVP: smartctl_exporter where actual disks are visible.
Enterprise: Scrutiny for specialist local history if validated; keep one source of disk metrics. No SMART promise for virtual EKS disks.

Limitations: IPMI's FreeIPMI dependencies and Redfish vendor/firmware differences need testing. Protect target parameters, management networks and credentials; some exporters perform pre-actions.
MVP: Prefer tested Redfish/fishymetrics for supported hardware; IPMI exporter fallback. Collect from a management segment using read-only accounts.
Enterprise: Maintain a certified vendor/firmware capability matrix; a small typed Redfish adapter may be safer than extending an exporter with write operations.

Alternatives and licences: [Healthchecks](https://github.com/healthchecks/healthchecks), BSD-3-Clause; [blackbox_exporter](https://github.com/prometheus/blackbox_exporter), Apache-2.0; Uptime Kuma evaluated in supplemental digest
Limitations: Missed push heartbeat and failed active probe are different evidence. A probe depending on the same failed Prometheus cannot detect its evaluator's death.
MVP: Healthchecks outside the cluster plus local independent API/freshness checker. Use blackbox probes for service reachability.
Enterprise: Separate regional failure domains, independent alert transports and an external observer of the fleet watchdog itself.

Limitations: Linear gauge forecasts are not general failure prediction. Libraries lack Nightshift's labels, feature pipeline, calibration and action policy.
MVP: Thresholds, sustained trends, freshness and time-to-exhaustion estimates with uncertainty.
Enterprise: River online models or PyOD offline comparisons in shadow mode, promoted only after time-ordered evaluation improves incident outcomes.

Limitations: Broad tools and default configurations can exceed Nightshift's permissions. No retrieved result establishes true causal accuracy or safe execution for this fleet. kagent is a larger agent platform.
MVP: K8sGPT analyzer baseline; restricted HolmesGPT as a parallel PoC. Fixed evidence tools, no shell/remediation credentials.
Enterprise: Adopt whichever beats deterministic baseline on representative cases; extend adapters upstream rather than maintain a broad fork. Defer kagent unless its lifecycle platform is independently needed.

Limitations: Opt-in instrumentation, sampling, local storage and sensitive attributes must be designed. Request bodies and trace names can reveal customer data.
MVP: Existing OTel instrumentation/backend only; do not mandate tracing for every cluster.
Enterprise: Compare local Jaeger/Tempo on actual traces; eBPF application capture such as Pixie is a separate consent/privilege evaluation.

Limitations: Controller is a library, not a complete safe-repair product. Argo needs template and parameter lockdown. Temporal needs durable services/datastore; StackStorm has a substantial dependency footprint.
MVP: Small controller owning typed repair resources and fixed compiled handlers. Argo is viable if already operated locally and locked down.
Enterprise: Temporal for long management workflows, or Argo for substantial local DAGs; local authorization still gates every mutation. StackStorm mainly if already the operations standard.

Alternatives and licences: [Medik8s NHC](https://github.com/medik8s/node-healthcheck-operator) + [SNR](https://github.com/medik8s/self-node-remediation), Apache-2.0; provider-native repair; typed Redfish recovery
Limitations: Partition handling, safe-state timeouts, minimum topology and privileged access are release-specific. Reboot is not application/data recovery.
MVP: Detection and escalation first; only catalogue-approved mitigation. Do not enable generic automatic fencing by default.
Enterprise: NHC/SNR or fence-agent integration after storage/fencing tests; provider-owned pools delegate node repair.

Limitations: Neither supplies durable approvals, truthful evidence or execution locking. Standalone OPA authentication is off by default.
MVP: Embed OPA in Go executor, default deny; test every catalogue action.
Enterprise: Cedar wins if entity-oriented authorization and existing team expertise dominate. Preserve a policy interface and conformance tests.

Alternatives and licences: Typed Nightshift approval service using existing IdP; Argo suspend/resume; Temporal signal-based workflow
Limitations: Suspend/resume and signals provide mechanisms, not customer delegation, exact-action binding or protection from replay. A timed resume is not consent.
MVP: Develop exact approval semantics; portal first, signed Slack requests through an adapter.
Enterprise: Workflow engine may host the wait; same local verifier, expiry and revalidation contract.

Limitations: Attribute filtering/PII detection does not guarantee confidential business context is removed. Redaction stability differs by signal.
MVP: Develop positive-schema fact builder and deny-by-default egress; optional redaction as another layer.
Enterprise: Domain-specific recognizers and privacy regression corpus; retain identical boundaries for fleet dashboards and inference.

Alternatives and licences: Direct provider adapters; [LiteLLM OSS](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm), MIT outside separate enterprise code
Limitations: Direct adapters require retries/quotas/compatibility work. LiteLLM adds keys, routing, logging and upgrades; some identity/audit controls are Enterprise.
MVP: Small adapter interface, fixed supported providers, request/token budget.
Enterprise: LiteLLM OSS if provider routing/quotas justify it; do not depend on commercial features accidentally.

Limitations: Runtime licence differs from model-weight licence. Context/concurrency consume KV memory. Local API and distributed runtime need security controls.
MVP: Benchmark llama.cpp or Ollama with approved quantized model; hosted sanitized mode remains a separate option.
Enterprise: vLLM for sufficiently utilized in-cluster accelerators and concurrency; no cross-cluster private inference until privacy policy permits it.

Limitations: GitOps can undo emergency changes if ownership overlaps. Repo/registry access and cold restarts fail during outages unless artifacts are cached.
MVP: Reuse existing GitOps; otherwise per-cluster Flux with digest-pinned signed OCI releases.
Enterprise: Shard release channels/cohorts; Argo CD where already standardized, with explicit HA/sharding.

Alternatives and licences: [OCM](https://github.com/open-cluster-management-io/ocm), Apache-2.0; Flux plus Nightshift metadata API; Argo CD cluster inventory
Limitations: OCM adds klusterlet/controllers and powerful work APIs; inventory alone does not provide safety or privacy. No reproduced 10k result here.
MVP: Existing Quornex inventory and a minimal status API; Flux for delivery.
Enterprise: OCM if placement/governance gaps justify it; cluster-local agents continue independently. Avoid duplicate fleet control planes.

Limitations: HTTPS requires custom retry/outbox. JetStream needs capacity/retention/account operations; message redelivery never means actions execute exactly once.
MVP: Batched outbound HTTPS and bounded local outbox.
Enterprise: NATS accounts, subject ACLs and isolated leaf domains for approved events; never bridge raw telemetry subjects.

Alternatives and licences: Kubernetes CRDs/status; [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/copyright.html), public domain; [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/about/licence/), PostgreSQL licence
Limitations: CRDs share API/etcd failure domain; don't store raw logs there. SQLite is a single-node persistence option, not replica-safe shared storage. Postgres needs backup/HA work.
MVP: CRD state for Kubernetes controller; SQLite only for a single-instance VM PoC or independent local outbox. Existing Postgres centrally.
Enterprise: Tenant-sharded Postgres, tested RLS and archive lifecycle; dedicated DB/instance for customers needing stronger isolation.

Limitations: Authentication does not establish repair approval/delegation. Central identity refresh can break offline approval workflows.
MVP: Reuse Quornex IdP; develop approval authorization separately.
Enterprise: Keycloak for full IAM; Dex for federation.

Limitations: Attested workload identity versus certificate management: distinct approaches, not interchangeable products. Test trust/expiry during disconnection.
MVP: Existing PKI and scoped service accounts; cert-manager if already present.
Enterprise: SPIRE when workload attestation and federation justify its control plane/agents.

Limitations: Online secrets service versus encrypted configuration files; different rotation/availability trade-offs. Neither guarantees offline credential continuity.
MVP: Encrypted Kubernetes Secrets; SOPS if Git carries secrets.
Enterprise: OpenBao when dynamic secrets/rotation warrant the service; retain local outage plan.

Limitations: Alertmanager groups/routes alerts; ntfy/Gotify supply push transports. Push is not guaranteed voice escalation; receipt is not approval.
MVP: Alertmanager + portal/Slack adapters; existing transports first.
Enterprise: Delivery receipts, escalation scheduling and independent phone transport; measure carrier/delivery costs.

Alternatives and licences: [Grafana](https://github.com/grafana/grafana), AGPL-3.0 core; native Quornex portal using backend APIs
Limitations: Grafana plugins/editions have separate terms. Native portal work costs development time. Neither is the local rule evaluator.
MVP: Existing Grafana for engineers; develop plain-language portal views.
Enterprise: Tenant-scoped queries, dashboard performance tests and customer evidence permissions.
